MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 17, 2026

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:02 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045
  Palos Verdes Drive N, Rolling Hills Estates, California, by VICE CHAIR POPE.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  VICE CHAIR POPE led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Pope, Johnson, Bain and McCormick

  Commissioners Absent:  Ciarolla, Holdsworth and Persichina

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REORGANIZATION PRESENTATION
  (VERBAL RERPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas informed the Commission that Mayor Zerunyan appointed
  Vice Chair Pope to be the 2026 Chair and Commissioner Ciarolla to be the 2026
  Vice Chair. She also noted Chair Persichina would be honored for serving as the
  2025 Chair at the next meeting.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 17, 2026

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  JOHNSON to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 17, 2026.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  1
MARCH 17, 2026
   6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROJECTS LIST

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a review of the capital improvements projects list (as
  per the agenda material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief review of a post closure land use plan and
  noted that many projects under consideration for Ernie Howlett Park would likely
  require a post closure land use plan, in response to COMMISSIONER BAIN.

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided an update regarding possible  restroom
  improvements at Ernie Howlett Park, in response to CHAIR POPE.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that a pickleball court assessment is included on the
  capital improvements projects list, in response to COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked about the open space at George F.
  Canyon. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff would add consideration of a park
  project at the open space near the Nature Center/George F. Canyon to the future
  projects list.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it is too early to be able to assess the impact of the
  new tennis and pickleball court play structure at the RHE Tennis Club on facility
  usage and related wear and tear, in response to COMMISSIONER JOHNSON.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)
  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief update regarding the 2026 Mayor’s
  Breakfast Ride scheduled for Saturday, May 9. He provided event details and
  timelines and noted that the local Scouts will again be serving breakfast at Ernie
  Howlett Park that morning.
  B.  HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief update regarding the 2026 Hills Are Alive
  5k/10k race scheduled for Saturday, May 30. He provided information regarding
  registration, marketing, sponsors, timelines, and other general event information.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  2
MARCH 17, 2026
   COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if the local Scouts would be interested in
  providing a breakfast service at the race as they do for the Mayor’s Breakfast
  Ride. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the Mayor’s Ride pancake breakfast
  provided by the Scouts is a large undertaking and may not be sustainable with
  the race being held so close to the Mayor’s Breakfast Ride but Staff would reach
  out to inquire if there is any interest regarding the Hills Are Alive.

  CHAIR POPE noted that Staff does provide free bagels, fruit, and water to all
  participants as they finish the race.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked if a stretching service could be provided
  similar to what is provided at the Jack Kramer Club during the Tracy Austin
  Tennis Tournament. Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the individual who provides
  that service charges for their time during the Tracy Austin Tennis Tournament.

  C.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)
  NONE.
  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON stated that an invitation had gone out regarding the
  Groundbreaking Ceremony for the new George F. Canyon Nature Center.

  CHAIR POPE stated that the South Bay Cities Council of Governments General
  Assembly is upcoming and encouraged Commissioners to consider attending, if
  possible.

  CHAIR POPE expressed gratitude for the service member banner program along
  Silver Spur Drive and provided positive feedback on the banners’ appearance.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 10, 2026

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF FEBRUARY 24, 2026

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK to:

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  3
MARCH 17, 2026
   RECEIVE AND FILE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  10.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR POPE ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:26 PM TO THE NEXT PARK
  AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON APRIL 21, 2026, AT 6:00 P.M.,
  WHICH WILL BE HELD IN THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CITY HALL.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  ___________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Lisa Van Ingen Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  4
MARCH 17, 2026
